source_text:
γάλα καὶ τοὺς μασθοὺς ἀψηλαφήτους ἐφύλαξεν, ἐβάστασε παιδίον καὶ τοῦ παι δίου
πατέρα οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν, ἐγένετο μήτηρ καὶ οὐκ ἐγένετο νύμφη. Υἱὸς ἐτρέφετο καὶ
πατὴρ οὐχ ηὑρίσκετο· ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκαρποφόρει καὶ ὁ καρπὸς γεωργὸν οὐκ ἐκέκτητο,
θέρος ἀπέδωκε καὶ σπόρον οὐκ ἐδέξατο· ποταμὸς ἔτρεχε καὶ ἡ πηγὴ πανταχόθεν ἐκέ
κλειστο, εἰς ἔνδειξιν ὅτι καὶ μήτηρ ἐγένου καὶ τὰ μητέρων οὐκ ἔπαθες· ἔτεκες ὡς
γυνὴ καὶ οὐκ ἐφθάρης ὡς γυνή· κατὰ νόμον ἐκυοφόρεις τῆς φύσεως, ἐπειδὴ τὸν
τεταγμένον καιρὸν τῶν ὠδίνων ἀνέμενες· ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ συνέλαβες παρὰ νόμον τῆς
φύσεως. Ἕτερός σε Πύλην κεκλεισμένην, ἐν ἀνατολαῖς δὲ κειμένην προσηγόρευσε
καὶ τὸν βασιλέα, τῶν θυρῶν κεκλει σμένων, εἰσάγουσαν. Οὕτω δὴ καὶ ἐκφέρουσαν
1
Πύλην σε κέ κληκεν, ἐπειδὴ θύρα τοῦ παρόντος βίου τῷ μονογενεῖ γέγονας, Πύλην
ἐν ἀνατολαῖς κειμένην, ἐπειδὴ «τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν τὸ φωτίζον πάντα ἄνθρωπον
ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον» ἐκ τῆς σῆς γαστρὸς καθάπερ ἔκ τινος παστάδος βασιλικῆς
προέρχε ται. Σὺ τὸν βασιλέα, τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, εἰσήγαγες, ἀλλὰ πάλιν
ἐξήγαγες· οὔτε γὰρ συλλαμβανόμενος, οὔτε ὅλως τικτόμε νος ὁ βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης
τὰς θύρας τῆς σῆς μήτρας ἠνέῳξεν, οὔτε τῆς παρθενίας τοὺς συνδέσμους ἐχαύνωσεν.
Σὲ «Κῆπον κεκλεισμένον» ὠνόμασε καὶ «Πηγὴν ἐσφραγισμένην» ὁ ἐκ σοῦ νυμφίος,
προεῖπεν ἐν τοῖς Ἄσμασι «Κῆπον κεκλεισμένον», ἐπειδὴ σοῦ μὲν δρεπάνη φθορᾶς ἢ
τρύγητος οὐχ ἥψατο, ἄνθος δὲ τὸ ἐκ τῆς ῥάβδου τοῦ Ἰεσσαὶ καθαρῶς τῷ γένει τῶν
ἀν θρώπων καὶ καθαρῶς παρίστησιν, ὑπὸ μόνου γεωργηθέν σοι τοῦ καθαροῦ καὶ
ἀκηράτου Πνεύματος· «Πηγὴν ἐσφραγισμέ νην», ὅτι ποταμὸς ζωῆς ἐκ σοῦ προελθὼν
τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐ πλήρωσεν, ἀλλὰ κλάδος γαμικὸς τὴν σὴν πηγὴν οὐκ ἤντλησε.
3 Περὶ σοῦ ∆αυὶδ τὸν ἐκ σοῦ κιθαρίζων οὐ παύεται· «Ἀνά στηθι, κύριε, εἰς τὴν
ἀνάπαυσίν σου, σὺ καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς τοῦ ἁγιά σματός σου.» «Ἀνάστηθι»· Πόθεν; Ἐκ τῶν
κόλπων τοῦ Πατρός, οὐχ ἵνα χωρισθῇς τοῦ Πατρός–τοῦτο γὰρ οὐ θέμις ἢ νοεῖσθαι ἢ
λέγεσθαι–, ἵνα δὲ τὴν οἰκονομίαν πράξῃς ἥτις ἄνωθέν σοι πρὸ αἰώνων καὶ πρὸ τῶν
γενεῶν προώριστο. «Ἀνά στηθι», ἵνα τοὺς πεσόντας ἐγείρῃς, ἵνα τοὺς σκελισθέντας
ὀρ θώσῃς, ἵνα τὸ σὸν ἀναλάβῃς κτῆμα, παρὰ τοῦ ἐχθροῦ μέχρι τοῦ νῦν
τυραννούμενον.
thought_title: Mary's paradoxical motherhood and the sealed gate
orientation: Hesychius continues his chain of biblical and natural paradoxes about Mary, then quotes Psalm 131 (LXX) as David's address to Christ, interpreting the ark as Mary.
pass_a_gloss: milk and the breasts [he] un-groped kept, [he] carried [a] child and of the child [the] father not [he] knew, [she] became [a] mother and not [she] became [a] bride. [A] son was being nourished and [a] father not was being found; the field was bearing fruit and the fruit [a] farmer not had acquired, [the] harvest gave back and seed not received; [a] river was running and the spring from every side had been shut, for [a] demonstration that both [a] mother you became and the [things] of mothers not you suffered; you gave birth as [a] woman and not you were corrupted as [a] woman; according to [the] law you were carrying in [the] womb of nature, since the appointed time of the birth pangs you were awaiting; but for also you conceived contrary to [the] law of nature. Another you [a] Gate shut, in [the] east but lying, addressed and the king, the doors being shut, bringing in. Thus indeed also bringing out [a] Gate you [he] has called, since [a] door of the present life to the only-begotten you have become, [a] Gate in [the] east lying, since "the light the true [one] the [one] illuminating every man coming into the world" out of your womb just as out of some bridal chamber royal comes forth. You the king, the doors being shut, brought in, but again brought out; for neither being conceived, nor at all being born the king of glory the doors of your womb opened, nor of the virginity the bonds loosened. You "[a] Garden shut" [he] named and "[a] Spring sealed" the out of you bridegroom, [he] foretold in the Songs "[a] Garden shut", since of you [a] sickle of corruption or of harvest not touched, [a] flower but the [one] out of the rod of Jesse purely to the race of men and purely presents, by only having been cultivated for you by the pure and undefiled Spirit; "[a] Spring sealed", because [a] river of life out of you having come forth the inhabited world filled, but [a] branch marital your spring not drew from. Concerning you David the out of you [one] playing [the] lyre not ceases: "Arise, Lord, into the rest of you, you and the ark of the holiness of you." "Arise"; From where? Out of the bosoms of the Father, not in order that you be separated from the Father – this for not [it is] lawful either to be thought or to be said –, in order that but the plan you accomplish which from above for you before ages and before the generations had been predetermined. "Arise", in order that the fallen [ones] you raise, in order that the stumbled [ones] you set upright, in order that the your possession you take back, by the enemy until the now being tyrannized.

lemmas.gloss: those who have been tripped up

choices.why: The adjective means 'not handled or touched'; 'untouched' preserves the negation and the sense of physical contact avoided, fitting the paradox of nursing without handling.
ἀπέδωκε is 'gave back/rendered/paid,' a financial metaphor; keeping 'gave back' preserves the paradox that summer/harvest rendered fruit without receiving seed, without adding 'produce.'

choices.term: Πύλην κεκλεισμένην, ἐν ἀνατολαῖς δὲ κειμένην
choices.english: a closed gate, and one lying in the east
choices.why: The source has two coordinated participial phrases modifying 'gate'; rendering both as appositive participles keeps the Ezekiel allusion's force and the source's word order.
rejected: a gate lying in the east, closed
a closed gate lying in the east

choices.english: not so that you would be separated
choices.why: The subjunctive χωρισθῇς is second person singular, with Christ as the subject of the whole address; 'you would be separated' keeps the second person and the passive sense.
rejected: not so that you would separate yourself
not for you to be separated

choices.why: παστάς is specifically a bridal chamber or inner chamber; 'royal bridal chamber' conveys both the regal and nuptial imagery Hesychius uses for Mary's womb.
κλάδος is 'branch' and γαμικός 'nuptial/marital'; the image is of a branch (perhaps a phallic or marital symbol) that did not draw from Mary's fountain; 'nuptial branch' keeps the metaphor literal.

bible_refs.note: Ἀνάστηθι, κύριε, εἰς τὴν ἀνάπαυσίν σου, σὺ καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς τοῦ ἁγιάσματός σου
τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν τὸ φωτίζον πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον

pass_b_english: she supplied milk and kept her breasts untouched; she carried a child and did not know the child's father; she became a mother and did not become a bride. A son was being nourished, and no father was to be found; the field was bearing fruit, and the fruit had no farmer; summer gave back, and received no seed; a river was flowing, and its source had been closed on every side—to show that you became a mother and did not suffer what mothers suffer. You gave birth as a woman, and you were not corrupted as a woman. You carried in the womb according to the law of nature, since you awaited the appointed time of labor pains; but you also conceived contrary to the law of nature. Another called you a closed gate, one lying in the east, and the one who brings in the king while the doors remain closed. So too he called you a gate that brings him out, because you became a door of this present life for the only-begotten—a gate lying in the east, because "the true light that enlightens every person coming into the world" (John 1:9) comes forth from your womb as from a royal bridal chamber. You brought in the king while the doors were closed, and again you brought him out; for neither in being conceived nor in being born at all did the King of glory open the doors of your womb, nor did he loosen the bonds of your virginity. The bridegroom who came from you named you "an enclosed garden" and "a sealed fountain"; he foretold in the Songs: "an enclosed garden," because no sickle of corruption or harvest touched you, but the flower from the rod of Jesse he presents purely to the human race, purely cultivated in you by the pure and undefiled Spirit alone; "a sealed fountain," because a river of life came forth from you and filled the world, but no nuptial branch drew from your fountain.

Concerning you David does not cease making music on the lyre about the one who came from you: "Arise, Lord, into your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctification" (Psalm 132:8, LXX Psalm 132:8). "Arise"—from where? From the bosom of the Father, not so that you would be separated from the Father—for that is not lawful even to think or to say—but so that you might accomplish the plan of salvation that was ordained for you from above before the ages and before the generations. "Arise," so that you may raise up those who have fallen, so that you may set upright those who have been tripped up, so that you may take back your own possession, which until now has been tyrannized by the enemy.

problems.quote: making music on the lyre for the one who came from you
problems.source_quote: τὸν ἐκ σοῦ κιθαρίζων οὐ παύεται
problems.why: τὸν ἐκ σοῦ is object of κιθαρίζων, not beneficiary: David plays 'the one from you' (Christ), not 'for' him.
problems.fix: David does not cease playing on the lyre the one who came from you
problems.ruling: κιθαρίζων takes direct object τὸν ἐκ σοῦ; 'plays the one from you' not 'makes music for'

problems.quote: the flower from the rod of Jesse presents itself purely to the human race, purely cultivated in you
problems.source_quote: ἄνθος δὲ τὸ ἐκ τῆς ῥάβδου τοῦ Ἰεσσαὶ καθαρῶς τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ καθαρῶς παρίστησιν, ὑπὸ μόνου γεωργηθέν σοι
problems.why: παρίστησιν takes double accusative: 'presents the flower purely to humankind'; 'purely cultivated in you' misplaces καθαρῶς and splits the syntax.
problems.fix: the flower from the rod of Jesse he presents purely to the human race, purely, cultivated in you by the pure Spirit alone
problems.ruling: παρίστησιν governs ἄνθος + τῷ γένει; 'presents itself' drops object; καθαρῶς misplaced to 'cultivated'

edits.old: making music on the lyre for the one who came from you
edits.new: making music on the lyre about the one who came from you

edits.old: the flower from the rod of Jesse presents itself purely to the human race, purely cultivated in you
edits.new: the flower from the rod of Jesse he presents purely to the human race, purely cultivated in you

fixed: Changed 'for the one who came from you' to 'about the one who came from you': source τὸν ἐκ σοῦ is object of κιθαρίζων, not beneficiary.
Changed 'presents itself' to 'he presents': source παρίστησιν has the bridegroom as subject, taking the flower as object, not reflexive.

sweep.held_why: 1 confirmed problems after 1 repairs; repair made no edit

dismissed.quote: the bridegroom who came from you
dismissed.why: ὁ ἐκ σοῦ means 'the one from you' i.e. Christ born from Mary, not 'who came from you' as visitor.
dismissed.note: 'The bridegroom who came from you' correctly means Christ born of Mary; there is no sense of a visitor.
